evidence.note: Recognized initial codebase was 'fundamentally flawed with many interconnected issues' and undertook a full from-scratch rewrite of all modules rather than continuing to patch — a decisive structural pivot when the first approach was falsified.

Diagnosed that the closure-based gen_lvalue pattern caused infinite type recursion at compile time and restructured codegen into separate gen_expr/gen_address paths — root-cause-driven redesign, not a symptom patch.

Found local declarations were being lost as identifier expressions; introduced a new Stmt::Decl AST variant and propagated it through parser/sema/codegen — a representation change to fix a structural limitation.

Diagnosed pointer segfaults as movl-vs-movq store-size bug and introduced type-aware sized codegen (get_expr_size) — distinguished a structural limitation (no size info) from a local bug and added proper type-size handling.

Explicitly recognized the parser was fundamentally inadequate for complex C types (nested anonymous struct/union, typedef) but chose to keep patching rather than redesign it — recognition of a dead end without full corrective action.

Repeated regressions: .note.GNU-stack fix lost on backup restore, recurring offset double-negative bug reappearing late — fragile sed/python patch workflow caused needless churn and the same root cause recurring.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds the level-5 anchor: it repeatedly diagnoses root causes and undertakes targeted structural redesign (full early rewrite, splitting codegen paths, introducing Stmt::Decl representation, adding type-aware sized operations) with explicit reasoning, matching much of the level-8 description. However it falls short of a clean 8/10 because it recognizes but patches around the fundamentally weak parser instead of redesigning it, and its fragile edit workflow produces the exact 'needless churn' and recurring-root-cause behavior (lost fixes, reappearing offset bug) that the high anchors warn against. This places it solidly between 5 and 8, at 6.
